meta.title: Coca-Cola's Best-Tested Product Ever Lasted Only 79 Days
meta.hook: Coca-Cola changed its 99-year-old formula. It lasted 79 days.
meta.description: In 1985 Coca-Cola replaced its original formula with 'New Coke' after blind taste tests showed it beating Pepsi and old Coke. The backlash was immediate: up to 8,000 calls a day and roughly 40,000 letters. On July 11, 1985 — 79 days after launch — the original formula returned as Coca-Cola Classic.

scenes.narration: In nineteen eighty-five, Coca-Cola changed its formula for the first time in ninety-nine years. It lasted seventy-nine days.

scenes.narration: The company had blind-tested New Coke against Pepsi and its own original formula. New Coke won those taste tests.

visual.visual_intent: Rows of small tasting cups on a table, clinical bright light, product-test aesthetic
visual.decision_reason: corroborated by Coca-Cola Company's own history page and multiple outlets

scenes.narration: But when it hit shelves on April twenty-third, people didn't just dislike it. They felt betrayed.

scenes.narration: On July eleventh, seventy-nine days later, Coca-Cola brought the original formula back as Coca-Cola Classic.

scenes.narration: The best-tested product in company history still lost, because taste wasn't what people were actually buying. Follow for more.
